definitions.explanation: Noticeably different from what is normal or expected in a way that is unsettling or disturbing. Stronger than simply unusual — implies something feels wrong or off-putting.

examples.japanese: {異様|いよう}な{雰囲気|ふんいき}だった。
{彼|かれ}の{異様|いよう}な{行動|こうどう}にみんな{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.english: Everyone was startled by his bizarre behavior.

examples.japanese: {深夜|しんや}の{公園|こうえん}から{異様|いよう}な{音|おと}が{聞|き}こえてきて、{思|おも}わず{足|あし}を{止|と}めた。
examples.english: I heard a strange sound coming from the park late at night and involuntarily stopped in my tracks.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a na-adjective ({異様|いよう}な) to describe things that are strikingly strange or unsettling. Often used to describe atmospheres, appearances, sounds, or behaviors that feel abnormal.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {異様|いよう}な{雰囲気|ふんいき} (eerie atmosphere)
- {異様|いよう}な{光景|こうけい} (bizarre sight)
- {異様|いよう}に{静|しず}か (eerily quiet)
- {異様|いよう}な{臭|にお}い (strange smell)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {奇妙|きみょう}: strange, odd (intellectual curiosity, less threatening)
- {不気味|ぶきみ}: creepy, eerie (specifically unsettling or frightening)
- {変|へん}: strange, weird (casual, milder)
